note: Paragraph 1622 of the old Tariff Act schedule (19 USC 1201) was repealed by Pub. L. 87-456 (1962); the definition was never conformed (References in Text note).
42 USC 1973c was editorially reclassified to 52 USC 10304 (2014); the enacted cite is stale and the Code adds a bracket "[now 52 U.S.C. 10304]".
26 USC 4761 (Marihuana Tax Act) was repealed in 1970; the only note is a Codification note on the 1954-Code substitution, and nothing flags the repeal.
1395mm(i)(6)(B) exists; the record indents the subsection heading "(i) Duration, termination..." as a roman-numeral clause, so the reader never sees subsection (i).
Pub. L. 110-411 enacted 4145c and rewrote 4112 in the same Act; the certification of compliance is now 4112(b)(2)(D), and the Code footnote says "So in original... does not contain a par. (4)".
Pub. L. 108-159 rewrote 1681g(c), which now has only paragraphs (1) and (2); the summary of rights is at (c)(1). The source was not conformed (References in Text note).
25 USC 450 et seq. (ISDEAA) was editorially reclassified to 25 USC 5301 et seq. in 2016; the enacted cite is stale (References in Text note).
The reader cut "300m–3(c)(2)" down to 300m(c)(2). The intended targets (300m-3 and 300o-2, the old health planning provisions) are also gone, so the law does dangle, just not at the parsed path.
1395x(iii)(2)(A) (home infusion therapy professional services) exists; the subsection heading "(iii)" is indented as a clause in the record.
42 USC 14135a was editorially reclassified to 34 USC 40702 (2017); the enacted parenthetical is stale (References in Text note).
16 USC 4107 (IFA section 308) was repealed by Pub. L. 117-328 (2022); 46 USC 12113(g) still cites it for vessels bought under that program (References in Text note).
(n)(1)(G) has no clauses; the patent certification with clause (iv) is now (n)(1)(H)(iv) after a later redesignation, and the cross-references were not conformed. No footnote.
22 USC 7536 (Afghanistan Freedom Support Act report section) was omitted from the Code in the 2012 edition (References in Text: "omitted from the Code").
5 USC 5532 (dual-compensation limitation) was repealed by Pub. L. 106-65 (1999) (References in Text note).
The source explicitly cites 20 USC 2471 "as such sections are in effect on August 22, 1996" (a historical version), so it is not a dangling reference to today's Code.
Old 31 USC ch. 67 (revenue sharing, incl. 6721) was repealed by Pub. L. 99-272 (1986). Today's 6701-6720 are a different, later chapter, so 6721(d) is gone (References in Text note).
637(d)(3)(C) exists inside the quoted contract clause of 637(d)(3); the record flattens the quoted "(A)"-"(H)" lines, so the reader misses them.
33 USC 1171 (pre-1972 FWPCA section 21) was "omitted as superseded" by the 1972 FWPCA rewrite (likely now 33 USC 1341) (References in Text note).
1715k(h)(8) exists; the clauses (i)-(iv) of (h)(2) are at top-level indent in the record, so the reader closes subsection (h) at "(i)".
15 USC 297(b)(A) exists after the "(1)/(2) ... shall—" lead-in; the reader nests (A) under (2) instead of directly under (b).
42 USC 12339 was repealed by Pub. L. 103-252 (1994); 12335 still lists it three times (References in Text note).
29 USC 32 (Vocational Rehabilitation Act of 1920) was repealed in 1973 and its references now run to the Rehabilitation Act (29 USC 701 et seq.) (References in Text note).
12 USC 101, 177 and 178 were repealed by Pub. L. 103-325 (1994) (References in Text note); 101 and 177 have no stub in the record.
The garbled text "sections 3675 paragraphs (1), (2), and (6) of section 3675(b), 3680A" attaches (6) to 3675(b), not 3680A; the reader built 3680A(6).
The statute itself says 1675c(e) was repealed by the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005; the reference is deliberate (References in Text note).
Pub. L. 114-255 restructured 247d-6b(c)(7), so old (C)(iii)-(v) are now (B)(iii)-(v); 300hh-10(b)(4)(J) still cites (C). No footnote.
1396d(a)(7) exists; the clauses (i)-(xviii) of (a)'s lead-in are at top-level indent, so the reader ends subsection (a) at "(i)".
20 USC 1486 (IDEA part D appropriations) was repealed by the 2004 IDEA rewrite (Pub. L. 108-446); 29 USC 772 still cites it, with no footnote or note.
1182(a)(6)(C)(i) exists; the line "(a) biological agent..." sits at top-level indent, so the reader closes subsection (a) early.
1182(a)(10)(B) (guardian for a helpless alien) exists; same early close of 1182(a) as A29.
